lines.text: Your agent spends an hour learning the tests need port five four three three. Tomorrow, a new session learns it again.
An agent task manager should remember for it. In Agent R Q, the workspace does.
Before it marks a task done, the agent saves one short note. It goes to the workspace memory.
The next task loads that memory first, and goes to the right port. The workspace gets smarter, not one session.
Every memory has a version. When two agents save at once, the stale save is refused.
So the agent reloads, merges, and saves version three.
Nothing is lost, and no agent writes over another.
Skills are the team's playbooks, switched on per workspace. One fix reaches them all.
An agent loads a skill only when its task needs it.
Bigger plans live on the Panno, and tick as the tasks finish.
Those are markdown docs that every workspace shares.
What does your agent relearn every morning? Tell us in the comments. Agent R Q is open source: try it at Agent R Q dot com.
